en: The Legend of the Elder Aḍḍhaceḷaka Sudhāvagga 3 The Legend of the Elder Aḍḍhaceḷaka In the past, during the time of the Buddha Kassapa, I was a weaver’s son who lived by the road. Seeing the Buddha, the Great Sage, approaching, I offered him half a garment. Because of that deed, I have been reborn in heaven for ninety-one eons. Having passed through those existences, I have now attained final Nibbāna. Through this very gift of half a garment, I have reached the state of an Arhat. By this merit, may I attain the supreme fruit of the Path. May I reach the state of a Buddha, the highest among all beings. May I become a Buddha, a teacher of gods and men. May I be one who brings peace to the world, a refuge for the world. May I be one who brings happiness to the world, a light for the world. May I be one who brings joy to the world, a shelter for the world. May I be one who brings delight to the world, a lamp for the world. May I be one who brings illumination to the world, a guide for the world. May I be one who brings liberation to the world, a leader for the world. May I be one who brings deliverance to the world, a protector for the world. May I be one who brings safety to the world, a savior for the world. May I be one who brings security to the world, a benefactor for the world. May I be one who brings welfare to the world, a friend to all beings. May I be one who brings benefit to the world, a source of bliss for all. May I be one who brings peace to all beings, a bringer of happiness to all. May I be one who brings joy to all beings, a bringer of delight to all. May I be one who brings satisfaction to all beings, a bringer of contentment to all. May I be one who brings empathy to all beings, a bringer of understanding to all. May I be one who brings insight to all beings, a bringer of wisdom to all. May I be one who brings knowledge to all beings, a bringer of enlightenment to all. May I be one who brings awakening to all beings, a bringer of realization to all. May I be one who brings liberation to all beings, a bringer of freedom to all. May I be one who brings release to all beings, a bringer of salvation to all. May I be one who brings emancipation to all beings, a bringer of deliverance to all. May I be one who brings escape from suffering to all beings, a bringer of Nibbāna to all. May I be one who brings the end of suffering to all beings, a bringer of peace to all. May I be one who brings the cessation of suffering to all beings, a bringer of bliss to all. May I be one who brings the end of delusion to all beings, a bringer of clarity to all. May I be one who brings the end of confusion to all beings, a bringer of discernment to all. May I
“I gave half a garment to the Blessed One Tissa;
I have become one who has reached the utmost wretchedness.”
I rejoiced in heaven for an eon.
wholesome deeds were performed by me.
Because I gave that poor-quality cloth at that time,
I do not know a miserable rebirth;
this is the fruit of giving what was poor.
there will be universal monarchs known as Samantacchadana.
There were thirty-two lords of men.
[He attained] the four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Aḍḍhaceḷaka speak these verses.
This is the third legend of the elder Aḍḍhaceḷaka.
